purpose: Ask Starters, single set for the Exec Dashboard Ask box, built for the office hours test. Customer-free.

starters.name: Book health
starters.what: The book by green, yellow and red health, what drives the red, and the 10 things to act on first.
starters.text: Review the health of active accounts for [teammate name, tier or all accounts]: how many are green, yellow and red on health (High, Average, Low), with ARR for each, and what is driving the red ones. Then give me the 10 call-outs to act on first, such as risk level 4 or 5, a renewal in the next 90 days, no touch in 30 days, or something in recent conversations the score does not show, with one next step each.
starters.watch: Do the green, yellow and red counts add up to your active accounts, and do the 10 call-outs match what you already worry about?

starters.name: Revenue at risk
starters.what: Total ARR at risk and how much renews in 90 days, then the 10 largest judged saveable, notice given or lost.
starters.text: How much ARR sits in active accounts for [teammate name, tier or all accounts] at risk level 4 or 5, and how much renews in the next 90 days? For the 10 largest, say whether each is saveable, has given notice (a churn event or a non-renewal email in the last 180 days), or looks lost, the main driver from the risk analysis, whether that analysis looks out of date, and where leadership should step in.
starters.watch: Does the ARR total match your own view, and does the saveable, notice given or lost call feel right on the top 10?

starters.name: Green but at risk
starters.what: Accounts that look healthy on the score but carry risk, the 10 largest with owner and driver, and the ones nobody will see coming.
starters.text: Which active accounts for [teammate name, tier or all accounts] show High health but are at risk level 4 or 5 or have a churn risk insight? Give the count, then the top 10 by ARR with owner, renewal date and the risk driver. Tell me which ones the owner is least likely to see coming (no decision maker touch in 90 days, or a score that recent conversations contradict) and the first move for each.
starters.watch: Is the risk real, or is the flag out of date? Quotes were cut mid-sentence in some test runs, so tell us if you see that.

starters.name: What's driving risk
starters.what: The 3 to 5 risk drivers that repeat across the 25 largest at-risk accounts, with count, ARR, examples and the one fix worth the most ARR.
starters.text: Read the risk analyses for the 25 largest active accounts for [teammate name, tier or all accounts] at risk level 4 or 5. Which 3 to 5 drivers repeat most, such as product issues, value perception, competitive pressure or stakeholder change? For each, give the account count, ARR and two example accounts, flag any analysis that looks out of date, then name the one fix that would protect the most ARR.
starters.watch: One test run came back without the tally of repeating drivers. Do the drivers ring true for your book?

starters.name: Churn lessons
starters.what: Why the last 25 churn notices happened, grouped and marked preventable, and 5 live accounts on the same path.
starters.text: What can we learn from churn notices in the last 180 days? Read the churn analyses for the 25 most recent accounts with a churn event, group the decisive reasons, mark each preventable or not, and say how many of those accounts are still active. Then name up to 5 active accounts for [teammate name, tier or all accounts] at risk level 4 or 5 showing the same pattern today, and why.
starters.watch: Do the preventable calls hold up, and are the 5 live accounts ones you would worry about?

starters.name: Renewal game plan
starters.what: Your next 90 days of renewals in three groups, with the at-risk ones judged for turnaround and a play on each.
starters.text: Sort active accounts for [teammate name, tier or all accounts] renewing in the next 90 days into at risk (risk level 4 or 5, churn risk detected, or a non-renewal notice in conversations), upsell potential (expansion readiness 4 or 5), and no risk signal, at risk first. For the 10 largest at risk, which can I still turn around (senior contact engaged in 60 days, recent win, time left), and what should I do on each?
starters.watch: The at-risk group changed between test runs. If you can, run it twice and tell us whether yours moves.

starters.name: Renewal reminder rules
starters.what: Renewals with no renewal discussion by tier, timing and owner, and a reminder rule: when it fires and who gets it.
starters.text: Which active accounts for [teammate name, tier or all accounts] renew in the next 90 days and carry the No renewal discussion insight? Give count and ARR, split by tier, by days to renewal (0 to 30, 31 to 60, 61 to 90), and by account owner against each owner's total renewals in the window. Is it concentrated or spread? Recommend an automated reminder: when it fires and who gets it.
starters.watch: One test run skipped the days-to-renewal split. Is the reminder rule one you would turn on?

starters.name: Contact change alerts
starters.what: Accounts with a contact change in 30 days, the ones that matter (renewing or at risk), who changed and on which side.
starters.text: Which active accounts for [teammate name, tier or all accounts] had a farewell or organization personnel change event in the last 30 days? Give count and ARR, and flag the ones renewing in the next 180 days or at risk level 4 or 5. For the top 10 by ARR, say who changed and whether it was on the customer's side or our own team. Recommend the play an automated alert should start.
starters.watch: Did the people it names really change, and is the customer side versus our side call right?

starters.name: Prep a 1:1
starters.what: One teammate's book in four numbers, a real win to open with, 3 accounts to raise and a coaching question for each.
starters.text: Prep me for a 1:1 with [teammate name]. Across [teammate name]'s active accounts: count and ARR, accounts at risk level 4 or 5, renewals in the next 90 days, and accounts with no touch in 30 days. Open with one real win from the last 90 days, then the 3 accounts I should raise and one coaching question for each.
starters.watch: Fill in a real teammate. Is the win it opens with real, and are the 3 accounts the ones you would raise?

starters.name: Team workload
starters.what: Every owner's book, at-risk ARR and renewal load, who is over the line, and the accounts behind each flag.
starters.text: Group active accounts for [teammate name, tier or all accounts] by account owner: account count, ARR, accounts at risk level 4 or 5, and renewals in the next 90 days. Show the 15 owners with the most at-risk ARR, flag anyone with more than 25 percent of their ARR at risk or 10 or more renewals in 90 days, and tell me where a manager should help first, naming the accounts behind each flag.
starters.watch: Owner totals sometimes included inactive accounts in testing. Do the flagged owners match what you know?

starters.name: Expansion pipeline
starters.what: AI-detected expansion opportunities by category and tier, how many are ready, and the 10 on your largest accounts to push.
starters.text: Break down AI-detected expansion opportunities on active accounts for [teammate name, tier or all accounts] by category and tier: how many opportunities and accounts in each, and how many are ready to advance (high confidence, heating, and budget approved or technically validated), developing or blocked. No dollar totals. Then list the 10 ready-to-advance opportunities on the largest accounts with offering, decision maker and timeline, and say where leadership should help.
starters.watch: The weak spots in testing were the category by tier breakdown and opportunity versus account counts. Tell us what a useful version would show you.

starters.name: Advocates to ask
starters.what: Accounts that praised you in the last 90 days, their words and dates, and the 3 best people to ask.
starters.text: Which active accounts for [teammate name, tier or all accounts] had exceptional positive events in the last 90 days? List the top 10 by ARR with what happened, when, and the customer's words, naming the speaker only when the message shows it. Then rank the 3 strongest advocate candidates, favoring no risk level 4 or 5, no churn risk and no open problem in recent conversations. Say what to ask each for and what to confirm first.
starters.watch: The list changed between test runs. Would you actually reach out to the 3 it ranks first?

starters.name: Topics to act on
starters.what: The 5 most negative topics with volume, accounts, negative rate and growth, each routed to product, enablement or process.
starters.text: Across active accounts for [teammate name, tier or all accounts] in the last 90 days, which topics with at least 100 mentions have the highest share of negative sentiment, and which grew most versus the prior 90 days? For the top 5, show mentions, accounts, negative rate and growth, then say whether each points to a product fix, an enablement need or a process change, with one short example each.
starters.watch: The Active filter was dropped on topic counts in testing. Do the 5 topics and the product, enablement or process call make sense?

starters.name: Competitor mentions
starters.what: Which accounts mentioned a competitor in the last 90 days, the context, and which look like an active evaluation.
starters.text: Which active accounts for [teammate name, tier or all accounts] mentioned a competitor in the last 90 days? For each, name the competitor, the context it came up in, when, and how they felt about it, naming who raised it only when the message shows it. Rank by what signals an active evaluation or dissatisfaction, and show the top 10 by ARR.
starters.watch: New for this session, so we have no test record in the app. Do the competitors and the evaluation calls match what you hear from your team?

starters.name: Data health check
starters.what: Count and ARR for six data gaps that weaken Ask answers, the 10 largest affected accounts, and fixes ranked by impact.
starters.text: Run a data health check on active accounts for [teammate name, tier or all accounts]: how many have no owner, no renewal date, a renewal date before today, no email connected, no meetings connected, or no AI summary? Give count and ARR for each, list the 10 largest accounts with any of these, and rank the fixes by how much they would improve what users get from Ask.
starters.watch: One test run read the sync flags wrong. Do the six gaps match what you see in your own instance?

starters.name: Signals to double-check
starters.what: Accounts where churn signals disagree, count and ARR, the 10 largest in each group with dates, and which to fix first.
starters.text: Find active accounts for [teammate name, tier or all accounts] where Staircase signals disagree, in two groups: a churn event in the last 180 days but no Churn Risk insight, and a Churn Risk insight with no risk level. Give count and ARR for each, then the 10 largest in each group with owner, latest churn event date and renewal date, and tell me which group to fix first and how.
starters.watch: One test run sized only one of the two groups. Does it cover both, and is the fix order sensible?

starters.name: Prep my call
starters.what: Where you left off, what each side owes, risks to be ready for, wins to raise, who's who, and 3 dated talking points.
starters.text: Prep me for my next call with [write the account name]. Where did we leave off, what do we owe them and what do they owe us, and what risk should I be ready for, including any churn risk detected? Which recent wins can I bring up, and who are the key people and where does each stand? Give me 3 talking points, each tied to a dated conversation.
starters.watch: Pick an account with a call coming up. Are the 3 talking points tied to real, dated conversations?

starters.name: Catch me up
starters.what: The 3 to 5 dated developments of the last 90 days, how their tone toward us changed, open asks, risk state and one next move.
starters.text: Catch me up on [write the account name] over the last 90 days. Give me the 3 to 5 developments that matter most, each with its date and source, what changed in how they talk about us and why, and any open asks on either side. Tell me the risk level (or that none is assessed) and whether churn risk is detected, then the one thing to do next.
starters.watch: Are the developments dated and sourced, and is the one next move something you would actually do?

starters.name: Risk and save plan
starters.what: Risk level and churn state from the record, the top 3 drivers in their words, a saveability call and a 30-day save plan.
starters.text: Is [write the account name] at risk? Take the risk level and health from the account record (say if there is no assessment), tell me whether churn risk is detected, and give the top 3 drivers in the customer's words, with dates. Then judge how saveable it is: a senior contact still engaged, a recent positive moment, and days left before renewal. End with a 30-day save plan.
starters.watch: Does it take risk and health from the record, and are the drivers in the customer's own words with dates?

starters.name: Path to Green plan
starters.what: Where the account stands, what is pulling it down, and 5 actions with owners and dates to turn it green.
starters.text: Build a Path to Green plan for [write the account name]. Say where it stands today on health and risk from the account record (or that there is no assessment), what is pulling it down in the customer's own words with dates, and what has to be true for it to turn green. Then give me the 5 actions that get it there, each with an owner (us or them), a first step and a target date in the next 60 days, and the one sign that tells me it is working.
starters.watch: New for this session. A Path to Green plan is the most shared prompt among real users, so we want to know if this version reads like something you would put in front of a manager.

starters.name: Executive briefing
starters.what: A one-screen brief before an executive conversation: standing, risk, their asks, commitments and what to say.
starters.text: Brief me on [write the account name] before I meet their executives: where the relationship stands, the risk level and whether churn risk is detected, what they have told us they need, open commitments on both sides, and the 3 things I should say. Keep it to one screen.
starters.watch: Is it really one screen, and would you say those 3 things to an executive?

starters.name: Taking over an account
starters.what: A handoff brief: why they bought, key people and stances, dated wins and problems, commitments, risk and your first 5 moves.
starters.text: I'm taking over [write the account name]. Give me a handoff brief: why they bought and what they want to achieve (say if the record does not show it), the key people (champion, decision maker, anyone pushing back) and where each stands, dated wins and problems from the last 90 days, open commitments on both sides, the risk level, whether churn risk is detected, and my first 5 moves.
starters.watch: Pick an account you know well. Is the brief accurate, and does it say so when the purchase history is blank?

starters.name: Escalation review
starters.what: A dated timeline of what went wrong, who is involved, promises kept or missed, and a recovery plan.
starters.text: [write the account name] is escalating. Give me a dated timeline of what went wrong in the last 90 days, who on their side is involved and how they feel, what we promised and whether we delivered, and the recovery plan you recommend.
starters.watch: One test run misdated a delivery. Check the timeline dates against what you know.

starters.name: Stakeholder map
starters.what: The 10 most engaged contacts, tagged versus real decision maker, who left or went quiet, and 2 people to reach.
starters.text: Who matters at [write the account name]? List the 10 most recently engaged contacts with role and last engaged date. Name who is tagged decision maker and who actually approves things in recent conversations, and flag anyone on their side who left, changed role or went quiet in the last 90 days. Then tell me where we are single-threaded and the 2 people to reach next, and why.
starters.watch: Both test runs gave a long table instead of a top 10. Is the real decision maker right?

starters.name: Draft my follow-up
starters.what: A short, warm follow-up email built from your latest meeting or thread, with the checklist and the sources it used.
starters.text: Draft a follow-up email to [write the account name] from my most recent meeting or email thread. First list what it must cover: open items, commitments on both sides, any concern to acknowledge. Then write it short and warm, in my voice, with clear next steps. Leave out pricing, ARR and renewal dates, and show me the conversations you used.
starters.watch: One test run stitched three threads together. Check the sources it lists before you would send anything.

starters.name: Signal audit
starters.what: Every stored signal on one account side by side, which ones are out of date, and what to fix.
starters.text: Audit the signals on [write the account name]: risk level, churn risk insight, churn or churn risk events in the last 180 days, renewal date and the latest renewal analysis, health and sentiment. Which agree, which look out of date against recent conversations, and what should be fixed in the data?
starters.watch: Which signals does it call out of date, and do you agree?
